section_entries.label: 1 From Richard Dedekind to Emil Artin
section_entries.mathematical_role: Traces the arithmetic/analytic inheritance, derives Artin's function-field zeta representation, formulates pRH as a root-modulus condition, and reviews finite computational cases.

unit_result_entry.title: Artin reduces a function-field zeta function to a finite root polynomial
unit_result_entry.why_material: Builds the quadratic function-field analogue through ideals and Euler factors, reorganizes it as a finite polynomial, connects its roots to prime counting and class numbers, and states pRH as a common root-modulus condition after removing trivial zeros.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Keeps the arithmetic construction, Dirichlet-character interpretation, reciprocity, factorization, and pRH normalization together.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Several symbols and denominators are degraded; exact formulas and the treatment of trivial zeros require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A self-contained polynomial arithmetic inherits an analytic zeta layer
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Shows how Dedekind's arithmetic analogy for polynomials modulo a prime coexisted with the analytic Dedekind-zeta side of number fields, creating the two-part template Artin would transfer.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Point counts recover Artin's tabulated root data
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Shows how Artin's roughly forty examples can be checked by counting curve points and converting the result to the coefficient or Frobenius trace used in the zeta polynomial.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The successful finite-field reframing packages extension-field point counts into a rational zeta function whose numerator roots are Frobenius eigenvalues; pRH is then an intrinsic norm statement accessible through endomorphism structure.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is an analogue in positive characteristic and does not by itself transfer a proof or operator to classical RH.
related_synthesis_entries.title: pRH becomes concrete when zeros are replaced by Frobenius and point counts

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Artin's crucial compression is that the quadratic function-field zeta problem becomes a finite polynomial root problem, so pRH is a common-modulus statement after trivial factors are removed.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source builds the quadratic extension through ideals and Euler factors, identifies a Dirichlet-character-like factor, uses finite coefficient relations to obtain a degree n-1 polynomial, connects its roots to prime counts and class numbers, and formulates pRH via their modulus.
directed.conceptual_reading: Finite-field periodicity converts an analytic zero-distribution question into finite algebraic data without eliminating its arithmetic consequences.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The coefficient sequence σν and root polynomial bridge Euler factors, quadratic reciprocity, zeta zeros, and counting formulas.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Trivial zeros and the relation between polynomial degree and curve genus require careful normalization; the extracted formulas are visibly degraded.
directed.uncertainty: The finite-polynomial mechanism is secure, but symbols, denominators, root conventions, and exact modulus statements need scan verification.

supported: The span constructs Artin's quadratic function-field zeta/L factor, introduces finite coefficients sigma_nu, obtains a degree n-1 root polynomial, links it to prime counts and class-number consequences, and formulates pRH after removing trivial zeros.
inference: Calling the polynomial a finite algebraic compression of an analytic zero problem is a sound conceptual reading of the reduction.

section_entries.label: 7 Hasse's second proof
section_entries.mathematical_role: Expresses pRH through Frobenius norm and the conjugating involution intrinsic to the endomorphism algebra.

unit_result_entry.title: Frobenius norm plus conjugating involution yields Hasse's second proof
unit_result_entry.why_material: Compresses the elliptic pRH proof into the identity between Frobenius and its conjugate and identifies the relevant anti-involution later called Rosati, replacing the first proof's lifting construction by intrinsic endomorphism structure.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The supersingular real-Frobenius case is explicitly flagged as requiring extra care.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Exact norm identities should be checked, but the structural mechanism is clear.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Changing the ground field invalidates a claimed supersingularity converse
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Diagnoses Hasse's conflation of a curve over an algebraic closure with its chosen finite-field Frobenius, gives supersingular counterexamples away from endpoint traces, and uses Honda-Tate conditions to state which quadratic Weil numbers actually arise from elliptic curves.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Higher genus forced a choice between analytic uniformization and structural algebra
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Contrasts Hasse's preference for a purely structural second proof with his initial proposal to generalize CM and abelian-function uniformization, then records Deuring's apparently decisive alternative.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Gauss-Herglotz and Hasse's first proof use characteristic-zero CM control followed by reduction, whereas the second proof and Deuring's higher-genus program seek an intrinsic algebraic positivity structure in Frobenius endomorphisms and correspondences.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: For higher genus the source explicitly says Hasse's proposed generalized norm step was never supplied; later success required other developments not covered here.

directed.boundary_or_failure: The supersingular real-Frobenius case is not covered by naive complex-conjugation intuition and requires separate treatment.
